evals.prompt: The owner explicitly asks you to implement Phase 1 after GF-010 has landed. There is no separate package qualification or external activation issue. GF-011, GF-012, and GF-013 are initially ready; GF-012 then becomes terminally blocked.
evals.expected_output: Treat the explicit current owner request as sufficient implementation authorization within the current product/design/track scope, start the operational ledger, and initially admit all three within capacity. Continue GF-011 and GF-013 while localizing the GF-012 block; GF-014 follows GF-013 and GF-015 waits for GF-011 and GF-014. Do not require a separate package review, digest approval, or external activation issue.
assertions: Treats the explicit current owner request as sufficient implementation authorization
Does not require package qualification, digest approval, or an external activation issue
States that GF-012 does not block GF-011 or GF-013 to GF-014, and that GF-015 waits for GF-011 and GF-014
Requires registered worktrees and continuous pairs

evals.prompt: A reviewed story is rebased onto the integration branch after another story lands. What must happen before integration?
evals.expected_output: The same pair creates a new committed candidate, runs every applicable required check with a minimal non-secret environment allowlist and exact ignored-state inventory, records ledger evidence, and performs incremental read-only re-review. It may use pnpm check:affected for local feedback but never as a substitute for the full pnpm check evidence required for candidate or integration gates.
assertions: Rejects transfer of the old verdict
Does not require a sealer or clone
Requires sanitized environment-name and ignored-state evidence without restoring a sealer
Rejects pnpm check:affected as a substitute for the full pnpm check evidence required for candidate or integration gates

evals.prompt: Recover a ledger-listed story worktree in three cases: its exact recorded branch/object exists and reconciles cleanly; the object is missing; or the surviving workspace is dirty/mismatched. Explain whether a fresh clone or hosted-CI checkout can be used.
evals.expected_output: Reattach the clean existing branch/object as a registered worktree; block the affected story for missing or dirty/mismatched facts while independent ready stories continue; use OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED only if recovery requires a material authority decision; reject a local clone and treat hosted CI only as independent CI infrastructure.
assertions: Starts with git worktree list porcelain reconciliation
Reattaches only an exact recorded branch and object at the registered path
Blocks only the affected story and descendants on missing objects or dirty and mismatched evidence
Uses OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED only when recovery requires a material authority decision
Rejects fresh-clone recovery and permits provider-managed checkout only for hosted CI
